reason: Local prerequisite lemma added because Stembridge Prop. 2.3 and its use in the heap criterion require that a convex chain, and in particular a covering pair, occurs consecutively in some linear extension. The contraction Q of the convex chain to a single vertex was checked for well-definedness: transitivity is inherited, and an antisymmetry cycle through the new vertex would produce c' <= x <= c with c,c' in the convex chain, forcing x into the chain; the expansion of a linear extension of Q gives the required linear extension of P. Depends on the previous lemma (existence of linear extensions) and on published def-partial-order, def-chain, def-graded-poset-and-rank (covering pairs). Source read: Stembridge Prop. 2.3 and its proof, Nadeau section 2.4 (convexity), Krattenthaler section 3.
